description:
First, isolated, fully-tested brick. No producer/consumer wiring yet — exercised only by its own unit tests so the tree stays green with zero dead-code warnings. ## Change Add `ReturnDemandMap

` to semantic.rs. It mirrors the contribution semantics of `ActivationInputMap

` without copying its older fact-ownership cache: per-key `contributors: HashMap` + `joined: RuntimeDemand`, with `conclude` (replacing arm) and `extend` (blocked-publisher arm). Key = `ExecutableKey`, value = `RuntimeDemand`. Important ownership split: the fact engine already owns job→fact output sets (`DependencyIndex::outputs`, `FactTable::{replace_outputs, extend_outputs}`). `ReturnDemandMap` should not duplicate that state. Its `conclude` receives the publisher's previous `ExecutableKey` outputs from the engine-facing caller and uses them only to retract stale content contributions; it returns the next output keys and changed keys for `World::complete_job` to translate into facts. ## Why `ReturnDemand(E)` is the backward dual of activation inputs: many publishers (callers), joined by lattice lub, revision bumps only when the join moves. The join op is `RuntimeDemand::join_assign` (semantic.rs:288) — the lattice already exists and is documented-monotone. The conclude/extend split is load-bearing: a blocked publisher must EXTEND (recant nothing), exactly as analyze_activation does for inputs. The fact-engine review matters here: publisher presence, previous output keys, dirty/settled state, and replace-vs-extend fact claims are already engine responsibilities. The semantic store owns only the joined payload needed to decide whether a cumulative fact's content moved. ## Rip out Nothing yet. Later, when `ContributionMap` lands, the older `ActivationInputMap` output-key cache should be collapsed onto the same engine-owned output-key handoff instead of preserving two ownership ledgers. ## Check Unit tests in semantic.rs (or a sibling test module): (a) two publishers' contributions join by lub; (b) retracting one publisher recomputes the join and reports the key changed only if the aggregate moved; (c) extend never lowers a standing contribution; (d) empty join == RuntimeDemand::ignore (bottom); (e) conclude uses caller-supplied previous output keys rather than an internal output-key cache. `cargo test --lib` green, zero warnings.
title: Runtime demand: ReturnDemand contribution store mirroring ActivationInputMap
